cards.explanation: The answer is that they won't see his face again without their brother. Judah, one of Jacob's sons, tells his father the man said, "You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you." That's the whole deal, plain as day. No brother, no meeting. I think the brothers felt that sentence in their stomachs the whole way home.

The answer is False. Judah gives his father two options, friends. Send their brother, and they'll go down and buy food. Don't send him, and he says, "…we will not go…" Then he repeats the man's warning right behind it. That's a man who wants to be heard.

The answer is telling the man they had another brother. Israel asks his sons, "Why did you tell the man you had another brother?" He's looking at what was said in Egypt. The brothers answer that the man questioned them in detail about their family, and they just answered him. I think nobody at that table was enjoying this conversation.

The answer is that Judah will personally guarantee Benjamin's safety. Judah says, "I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible." Then he adds that if he doesn't bring Benjamin back and set him before his father, he'll bear the guilt all his life. Judah puts himself on the line, friends. No extra helpers, no fine print.

The answer is True. Judah says, "If we had not delayed, we could have come and gone twice by now." He's pointing out that all this waiting has cost them. It's like hitting snooze three times and then asking why the whole morning is gone. He's not wrong, though.

The answer is honey, almonds and myrrh. Israel's list is "…a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds." These are some of the best products of the land, packed up as a gift for the man. Somebody was packing with care.

The answer is double. Israel says, "Take double the silver with you so that you may return the silver that was put back into the mouths of your sacks." So they bring the first silver back and more to buy food. Then he adds, "Perhaps it was a mistake." That's a father covering every angle, friends.

The answer is True. Israel says it just as written: "May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release your other brother along with Benjamin." He says it to his sons. The other brother is the one kept back in Egypt (Genesis 42:24). I think a father sending his sons off with those words is doing what he can.

The answer is that he's ready to accept losing his sons. Israel says, "As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved." I think he's bracing himself for the worst. Just before that he says, "May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man…" That's not an easy thing for a father to say out loud.

The answer is to take them to his house and prepare a meal. Joseph, the man in charge in Egypt, tells his steward, "Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they shall dine with me at noon." It's a dinner order, friends. The brothers get frightened once they're taken to the house (Genesis 43:18).

The answer is True. The brothers say it themselves: "They intend to overpower us and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys." They link it to the silver found in their bags the first time. Donkeys included. Nobody's getting left out of this plot in their heads.

The answer is their father's God. The steward says, "Your God, the God of your father, gave you the treasure that was in your sacks. I received your silver." He tells them not to be afraid. That's a calm answer for men who came in braced for the worst.

The answer is Simeon. The steward brings Simeon out to the brothers. He's the brother who was kept in Egypt (Genesis 42:24). The steward says it's fine, and then Simeon walks out. I think that's about the best way to hear "Do not be afraid."

The answer is that they bow to the ground before him. The text says it right after the gifts: "…they presented him with the gifts they had brought, and they bowed to the ground before him." Joseph is the man they've been so nervous about, friends. They come in humbly.

The answer is False. The brothers tell Joseph, "Your servant our father is well. He is still alive." Joseph had just asked, "Is he still alive?" So the answer they give is yes, and they bow down to honor him after saying it.
The answer is tears. The text says Joseph "…was moved to tears for his brother…" and went to a private room to weep. I think seeing Benjamin hit him hard. It's a tender moment, so let it be tender.

The answer is that eating with Hebrews was detestable to the Egyptians. The text says, "…the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them." So Joseph, his brothers and the Egyptians were each served separately. Same house, separate servings, friends.

The answer is True. The text says the brothers were seated in order by age, "…and the men looked at one another in astonishment." It doesn't say why. I'd be staring too if a seating chart got everybody's age right.

The answer is that Benjamin's portion was five times larger than any other. The text says, "…Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of the others." Five times, friends. If those portions were cookies, that's five on his side for every one on theirs. Then they all feasted and drank freely with Joseph.
